data.hypothesis: Using a single full warp for all 2 <= n <= 128 may avoid the shared-memory barriers of the existing 128-thread CTA: each lane performs up to four bounded loads, then the existing warp sum writes directly to out. This contrasts with the prior warp-only-through-32 variant. Keep n=1 on the baseline no-kernel device-to-device copy path; the supplied aggregate timings do not isolate n=1 or establish a per-size crossover.

memory_lessons.applicability: The timings are aggregate evidence only; use them to motivate a contrasting candidate, not to infer which individual sizes improved.
memory_lessons.claim: The direct-128 candidate and warp-through-32 candidate both passed all 10 recorded cases. Their three-sample means were 46.48 and 46.65 microseconds respectively, compared with the baseline's 46.67 microseconds; these results do not isolate per-size effects.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this full-warp-through-128 variant with the complete correctness set and repeated timings, then compare its aggregate result and any available per-size timing with the prior candidates.

memory_lessons.applicability: Preserve the n=1 path unless measurements show a better alternative; the baseline's no-kernel copy is a relevant comparison, but aggregate data alone cannot demonstrate its per-size performance.
memory_lessons.claim: The baseline uses an asynchronous device-to-device copy for n=1 and passed both recorded n=1 seed cases. Available timing results are aggregate rather than n=1-specific.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: If per-size timing is available, compare the unchanged n=1 copy route directly with a one-CTA alternative before changing that route.

data.notes: This is a candidate crossover policy, not a measured conclusion: n=1 remains on the baseline no-kernel copy route, n=2..128 uses one warp, and larger inputs retain the hierarchical fallback. The 128-element bound is the capacity of four bounded loads per lane, not a test-size specialization. The supplied aggregate measurements show two valid but semantically distinct candidates; none isolate per-size timing or establish a crossover. The controller should run all correctness cases and repeated timings before selecting a path.
transformations: For 2 <= n <= 128, use a single 32-thread CTA: each lane conditionally accumulates input[lane + j*32] for j=0..3, performs the existing full-warp integer sum, and writes directly to out.
Preserve the n=1 asynchronous device-to-device copy path and retain the existing hierarchical reduction for larger sizes.
